hypothesis: Replacing the quadratic pairwise at-most-one clauses in the full scope-111 one-hot DTS CNF with exact linear-size sequential counters will reduce clause overhead and let Kissat produce a validator-accepted witness within the bounded solver run.
rationale: The prior full-domain formulas spend substantial size on pairwise at-most-one constraints for one-hot marks and difference occurrences: the symmetry-strengthened formula has 2,383,982 clauses and remains UNKNOWN. Sinz sequential counters preserve exact at-most-one semantics with linear clause growth, directly testing whether clause representation—not the DTS decision problem or missing symmetry—dominates the timeout. The previously validated complete row-lexicographic and reflection symmetry breaks are retained.
expected_information_gain: SAT followed by independent verification would produce true-objective progress at scope<=111. UNSAT would certify only the finite frozen scope-111 instance. UNKNOWN or timeout would close this exact sequential-counter encoding at the declared budget and would not establish infeasibility.
method: Generate a DIMACS CNF for seven normalized six-mark rows with positive marks one-hot in 1..111, exact sequential-counter at-most-one constraints for all mark and difference-occurrence families, strict within-row order, complete lexicographic ordering of all five positive-mark coordinates between adjacent rows, the per-row reflection rule a1+a4<=a5, one auxiliary literal for each possible within-row difference occurrence, and exact sequential counters across all occurrences of each difference. Run Kissat 4.0.3 under WSL2 Ubuntu with a 120-second solver limit. Decode any SAT model using the preserved mark-variable IDs and independently validate it with the repository integer verifier and flat-counter verifier.
metric: SAT status, formula variables and clauses, sequential-counter auxiliary count, elapsed time, decoded rows, and independent DTS validity
metric_relation_to_true_objective: A decoded assignment accepted by both independent integer verifiers with scope<=111 is exactly true-objective progress. UNSAT establishes finite full-instance infeasibility only; UNKNOWN or timeout establishes no mathematical infeasibility.

configuration.encoding: one-hot marks plus explicit difference-occurrence auxiliaries and Sinz sequential at-most-one counters
configuration.symmetry_break: complete row lexicographic order plus per-row reflection a1+a4<=a5

kill_condition: Stop at SAT, UNSAT, or the 120-second Kissat limit plus bounded process cleanup. Do not infer mathematical infeasibility from UNKNOWN or timeout.

baseline_comparison.expected_relation: strict improvement only if SAT model passes both independent verifiers

previous_best_comparison.full_pairwise_kissat: UNKNOWN under 120-second budget with 15540 variables and 1461683 clauses
previous_best_comparison.expected_relation: same finite decision problem and symmetry breaks, but exact linear-size AMO representation

interpretation: Kissat returned UNKNOWN at the declared 120-second limit on the exact sequential-counter formula. No model was emitted, so the target was not reached and no mathematical infeasibility follows.
failure_mode: The exact sequential-counter encoding remained unresolved at the bounded Kissat solver limit; this is a solver-budget result, not an UNSAT certificate.
what_was_learned: The sequential counters reduced the formula from 2,383,982 to 1,610,283 clauses and used 332 MB peak resident memory, but Kissat still returned UNKNOWN after 119.64 solver seconds. Thus the prior full-domain timeout is not explained solely by pairwise at-most-one clause overhead. The primary and independent verifiers both rejected the empty decode because no assignment was available.
recommended_next_action: Close this sequential-counter Kissat budget as inconclusive. Do not infer finite or global DTS infeasibility; reallocate only to a materially different structural construction, exact encoding/capability, or human-supplied mechanism.
repetition_justification: This is not a repeat of the prior full Kissat/CaDiCaL experiments: it changes the at-most-one representation from quadratic pairwise clauses to exact sequential counters while preserving the same frozen finite DTS instance and the already-tested symmetry rules.
